processing: A needle-shaped green tea from early-spring buds and leaves, combining traditional handling with modern finishing; producers also use cold storage to keep it fresh.
harvest_season: Early spring, when the buds are used for the premium lines.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, round, straight needles, emerald with visible white down, like frosted pine needles.
appearance_wet: Tender, even, bright leaf that tends to stand upright in the glass.
taste_profile: A high, lasting, refreshing aroma with a fresh and mellow cup.

brewing.notes: Use a tall glass if you can. The needles stand and drift as they open, which is half of the appeal.

vintage_note: A green sold mainly as fresh spring tea, so look for the current year and drink it within about a year. The producer's range extends to jasmine versions, which are a separate scented product with their own quality points.
description:
Guang'an Songzhen, or pine needle, is a green tea from Longtan in the Guang'an area of eastern Sichuan, grown towards the Huaying Mountains. The name describes the leaf: thin straight needles with a coat of white down, likened to pine dusted with frost.

It is made from early-spring buds and leaves, and the premium value lies in the shape and freshness. Producers also advertise cold storage to hold it close to fresh through the year.

In the cup it offers a high, lasting fragrance and a fresh, mellow taste. Brew it in a glass to watch the needles stand, and use water slightly below the boil.

The name covers a family of products: Songya, Songlü and jasmine or orchid-scented Songzhen among them. Read the label closely, as they are not the same tea at the same grade.
history:
Songzhen is documented as a modern award-winning product. It won a Sichuan provincial quality award in 1994, a gold medal at the second China Agricultural Expo in 1995, and in 1997 a China Tea Science Society quality award alongside a brand title at the third Expo. A Songya line took a gold medal at the Chengdu international tea expo in 2000.

Earlier history, and the date of its first production, is not clearly documented.
